item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is the preferable starting point because its retry behavior and tests are safer and more directly exercise replayed multipart uploads, but neither patch satisfies the frozen contract and neither is merge-ready.","reasons":["B tests `Files.Upload` through a 429 retry using an `os.File` source and verifies both multipart attempts are identical; A tests retrying `Files.Add` but never verifies `Upload` itself retries.","A's global `makeBodyReplayable` buffers every request body and silently ignores `io.ReadAll` failures after consuming the reader, which can send a truncated body and hide the source error. B leaves non-seekable readers alone and returns relevant rewind failures.","Both candidates use the wrong public signature (`AddFileOption` or `UploadFileOption` instead of `FilesOption`), bypass `FilesService.Add`, add explicitly forbidden association fields, extend `multipartbody` instead of directly reusing `NewFile`, refactor generic retry handling, and omit the required source-reader-error test.","B's multipart and retry assertions are more comprehensive, including filename, field name, content, headers, associations, content length, and complete retry-body equality."],"risks_a":["Silently swallowed body-read errors can corrupt requests.","Unbounded buffering is applied globally to unrelated request bodies.","`Upload` duplicates `Add` request and response handling instead of delegating to it and has no retry test of its own."],"risks_b":["Changes existing option-constructor return types and introduces several forbidden public association APIs.","Seek-based `GetBody` reuses one underlying reader rather than returning an independent copy and changes transport closing semantics.","Contains substantial unrelated documentation and retry-transport scope, while still missing the exact required API and source-reader-error test."]}
